title: Cline vs Continue
summary: Compare coding assistants by model control, permissions and channel-specific lifecycle evidence.

sections.heading: Resolve the distribution channel first
paragraphs: Continue's README says its repository is read-only and describes a final 2.0.0 release; GitHub Releases lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release from 2026-06-19, npm lists CLI 1.5.47 from 2026-06-18, and JetBrains Marketplace says CLI development is active. These channel/version statements do not establish current CLI maintenance or support. Verify the selected package, publisher, update channel and security response before relying on it.

sections.heading: Test permission and model paths
paragraphs: Use the same repository task and model provider where possible. Record which actions require approval, where inference runs, what credentials are needed and which external services receive code or prompts.

sections.heading: Treat local inference as a separate test
paragraphs: Both profiles contain model-configuration information, but configuration support does not prove that a particular local model will meet quality, latency or hardware needs. Test a representative change and inspect the resulting diff.

pros.text: Cline documents local STDIO and remote MCP servers and supports server management in its IDE extension and CLI.
Continue documents configurable MCP servers as custom tools in Agent mode.

cons.text: Continue's documentation limits MCP use to Agent mode, so this capability is not documented across all modes.

Continue's README calls the repository read-only and 2.0.0 its final release; Releases lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release from 2026-06-19, npm lists CLI 1.5.47 from 2026-06-18, and JetBrains Marketplace says CLI development is active. These channel/version claims do not establish current CLI support or security response.

faqs.question: Can Continue use MCP outside Agent mode?
faqs.answer: No. Continue's MCP documentation says MCP tools are available only in Agent mode.

faqs.question: What do Continue's published artifacts say about CLI support?
faqs.answer: The README calls the repository read-only and 2.0.0 its final release; GitHub Releases lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release from 2026-06-19, npm lists @continuedev/cli 1.5.47 from 2026-06-18, and JetBrains Marketplace says CLI development is active. This does not establish current CLI maintenance, a support commitment or a security-response path for a selected package.

faqs.question: Which MCP transport does Cline recommend?
faqs.answer: Cline marks Streamable HTTP as recommended and SSE as legacy; match the transport to the server you intend to use.

faqs.question: What do Cline's public sources say about telemetry defaults?
faqs.answer: Cline's Terms, last modified 2025-09-25, say extension telemetry is on by default and can be disabled in settings; its 2025-02-26 blog describes telemetry as opt-in. These public statements conflict, so verify the current extension version and setting.

faqs.question: Can Continue be configured for offline use?
faqs.answer: Continue documents a VS Code setup that installs the extension, disables Allow Anonymous Telemetry and configures a local model. This documents a setup path, not the behavior of a specific build or every Continue channel; verify the selected package and provider separately.

verdict: Evaluate the exact package and support channel before comparing feature fit. The public CLI package/version history and a later VS Code pre-release narrow the channel record, but the README and Marketplace statements do not establish current CLI maintenance or a package-specific support commitment.
bestFor: Developers deciding how much model configuration and maintenance risk they can own
notFor: Teams that require a current upstream support commitment without first checking the package lifecycle
migration: Pin the current package version, export model configuration and preserve a working fallback. Reassess extension publisher and update state before each upgrade.
gaps: Current Continue CLI maintenance and security response remain unresolved: its README says read-only/final, the Marketplace says CLI development is active, GitHub Releases lists a 2026-06-19 v2.1.0-vscode pre-release, and npm lists CLI 1.5.47 published 2026-06-18. Confirm the selected package, publisher, update path and support response.

Continue's 2026-02-05 Privacy Notice does not establish its applicability to the post-acquisition product or processing when acting as a customer's processor; verify the selected package, account and model-provider route.
No local-model quality, privacy or performance trial has been performed.
Cline's actual telemetry configuration and selected-provider data handling were not inspected.
